page7_img_1.png.title: Number of developers resolving benchmark issues (Mylyn vs Eclipse Project)
page7_img_1.png.description: Table showing, for each system, how many benchmark issues were resolved by 1, 2, or 3 developers and the total issues considered. For Mylyn: 277 issues were resolved by a single developer, 21 by two developers, and 3 by three developers (total 301), meaning ~92% were single-developer resolutions. For Eclipse Project: 70 issues were single-developer, 0 by two developers, and 2 by three developers (total 72), meaning ~97% were single-developer resolutions. These counts match the paper’s benchmark composition used for the evaluation.

page5_img_2.png.title: Top five developers recommended by iHDev for Bug #313712
page5_img_2.png.description: A ranked list of the top five attachers (developers) recommended by iHDev for Mylyn bug #313712, showing each developer’s computed Score and final rank (cutoff m=5). The entries are: Frank Becker — Score 8.51 (rank 1); Steffen Pingel — 5.64 (rank 2); Robert Elves — 2.75 (rank 3); Jingwen 'Owen' Ou — 2.13 (rank 4); Shawn Minto — 2.00 (rank 5). Scores are the sum of xFactor contributions across the relevant files (higher score indicates greater interaction-based expertise); Frank Becker, who has the highest score, is the actual developer who fixed the bug, so iHDev placed the correct developer first.

page3_img_1.png.title: Mylyn InteractionEvent XML for an edit on TaskListView.java
page3_img_1.png.description: An XML snippet of a Mylyn InteractionEvent (for bug #330695, trace ID #221752) showing metadata captured during an edit session. The element records Kind="edit", StartDate="2013-01-13 19:34:01.900" and EndDate="2013-01-13 20:02:21.517 CET", Interest="34.0", and OriginId="org.eclipse.jdt.ui.CompilationUnitEditor". The StructureHandle points to the edited Java source (TaskListView.java and the TaskListView~makeActions context) and StructureKind="java", while NumEvents="34" and CreationCount="227" report the number of interaction events and the trace creation count.

page3_img_2.png.title: Interaction-log XML snippet for Bug #315184
page3_img_2.png.description: The image shows an XML snippet of an interaction-log entry for BugId 315184 with AttachId 196936 and Attacher name Steffen Pingel. It records an InteractionEvent with EndDate 2011-05-31 and Kind edit, and a StructureHandle that references the source file AbstractTaskRepositoryPage.java. The paper uses records like this (attacher, date, and file path for edit events) to build interaction logs and compute attacher–file measures (I_f, A_f, R_f) for the iHDev developer-recommendation approach.

page5_img_table_1.png.title: Top‑10 relevant files and attachers (xFactor) for Bug #313712
page5_img_table_1.png.description: Table listing the top ten source files (rank 1–10) identified as relevant to bug #313712 and, for each file, the attachers (developers) with their per‑file xFactor scores. Examples: rank 1 TaskEditorNewCommentPart.java shows Jingwen ’Owen’ (1.23) and Frank Becker (1.06); rank 3 NewAttachmentWizardDialog.java lists Frank Becker (1.40); rank 6 BugzillaResponseDetailDialog.java has a single high score Frank Becker (3.00); rank 7 UpdateAttachmentJob.java shows Frank Becker (1.94) and Robert Elves (1.40); rank 2 CopyContextHandler.java lists Shawn Minto (2.00). Two files (Messages.java, WebBrowserDialog.java) have no attachers listed. The per‑file xFactor values in this table were summed across the ten files to produce overall developer scores (the paper notes Frank Becker’s total Score = 8.51, explaining why he is recommended first).

page5_img_1.png.title: Top-five developer recommendations for bug #313712 by four approaches
page5_img_1.png.description: A four-row table compares the top-five ranked developers returned by iHDev, xFinder, xFinder' and iMacPro for bug #313712. iHDev lists Frank Becker in rank 1 (highlighted in red) followed by Steffen Pingel (2), Robert Elves (3), Jingwen ’Owen’ Ou (4), and Shawn Minto (5). The other approaches commonly place Steffen Pingel at rank 1 while Frank Becker—the actual fixer—appears lower (xFinder: rank 3; xFinder': rank 4; iMacPro: rank 3), illustrating that iHDev placed the correct developer highest among the compared methods.

page8_img_table_vi.png.title: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) comparison of iHDev vs baselines
page8_img_table_vi.png.description: The table reports MRR scores for iHDev, xFinder, xFinder', and iMacPro on two systems (Mylyn and Eclipse Project), and shows percent MRR gain, p-values (One Way ANOVA), and which approach is advantaged. For Mylyn iHDev has MRR=0.66 versus 0.56 (xFinder), 0.62 (xFinder'), and 0.64 (iMacPro), corresponding to gains of 17.85%, 6.45%, and 3.12%; only the improvement over xFinder is statistically significant (p=0.003). For Eclipse Project iHDev has MRR=0.34 versus 0.16, 0.16, and 0.17 for the three baselines (gains 112.5%, 112.5%, and 100%), all with significant p-values (0.005, 0.007, 0.01) and iHDev marked as the advantaged approach. (Higher MRR indicates the correct developer appears earlier in the ranked recommendations.)

page8_img_table_v.png.title: Recall@m comparison of iHDev versus commit-based approaches
page8_img_table_v.png.description: Table V reports recall@1, @2, @3 and @5 for four recommendation algorithms (iHDev, xFinder, xFinder', iMacPro) on two benchmarks (Mylyn and Eclipse Project), plus percent recall gains, ANOVA p-values and which approach is statistically advantaged. Absolute recall for iHDev is: Mylyn {0.50, 0.71, 0.79, 0.86} for m={1,2,3,5} and Eclipse {0.25, 0.37, 0.41, 0.45}; recall increases with m for all methods. Relative gains are typically positive and often statistically significant: for Eclipse iHDev yields very large gains (e.g., +127.27% vs iMacPro at m=1, p=0.02; +125% vs xFinder at m=5, p=0.001), while for Mylyn iHDev shows significant improvements for m≥2 (e.g., +16.17% vs xFinder at m=3, p=0.001), though at Mylyn m=1 differences are small and not significant. The table thus shows iHDev most consistently improves recall over the commit-based baselines, with accompanying p-values indicating significance in most comparisons.
